articles.title: Bateria do notebook: deixar na tomada o dia todo faz mal? | G1
articles.standfirst: A bateria tem vida útil limitada mesmo sem uso, mas a forma como você carrega o notebook pode acelerar ou evitar esse desgaste.
articles.summary: Veja o que acontece com a bateria ao deixar o notebook na tomada o dia todo e entenda os riscos para o aparelho a longo prazo.
articles.body:
Deixar o notebook na tomada o dia todo estraga a bateria? — Foto: TheRegisti/Unsplash

De forma geral, deixar o notebook na tomada o dia todo não vai desgastar mais a bateria do que deixá-lo passar pelos ciclos de descarregamento e carregamento.

Mas isso não é consenso entre as marcas e pode ter outras consequências, como diminuir a vida útil dos outros componentes, caso o dispositivo fique ligado por longos períodos.

🔋 O que acontece com a vida útil da bateria se ficar na tomada o dia todo?

É importante entender que a vida útil da bateria gira em torno de dois principais fatores: o tempo de vida dos componentes e os ciclos de carga e descarga aos quais ela é submetida.

“Estando em operação ou não, as baterias têm um tempo de vida limitado”, afirmou Bruno Lima, coordenador do curso de engenharia da computação da Universidade Presbiteriana Mackenzie, em entrevista ao g1 em 2025.

Segundo o engenheiro, dependendo do fabricante e da qualidade dos componentes, essa durabilidade "pode variar de 2 a 3 anos”. Ou seja, mesmo sem uso, a bateria sofre desgaste natural ao longo do tempo.

Mas o número de vezes que você carrega e descarrega normalmente o dispositivo – chamadas de ciclos – também pode influenciar a longevidade dele. Conforme aumenta a quantidade de ciclos, a bateria não tem mais o mesmo desempenho.

Em notebooks mais antigos, a bateria continuava sendo consumida mesmo com o aparelho na tomada. "Em modelos mais novos, o sistema consome a energia direto, sem passar pela bateria ", disse Ricardo Ciuccio, coordenador do curso de engenharia da computação do Centro Universitário Senac.

“O fato de ele estar sempre na tomada vai fazer com que essa bateria retenha a carga. Não vai ter um efeito significativo no tempo de vida além dos ciclos normais de carga e recarga ”, explicou Lima.

No entanto, os especialistas chamam atenção para os efeitos negativos para as outras partes do computador.

“Quando você deixa ele ligado por dias, você está mantendo os componentes energizados, está passando corrente, ele está aquecendo. Isso pode degradar a vida útil dos componentes”, explica Lima.

Ciuccio aponta que o calor gerado pela bateria com a carga completa pode também danificar os componentes. "Quando está carregada, esse calor vai tirando uma fração de tempo da durabilidade da bateria", comentou.

"É aí que tem divergências entre fabricantes. Você vai encontrar manuais que são favoráveis a manter o notebook na tomada e outros que não são", completou Ciuccio.

📄 Sempre confira a recomendação da fabricante

Além do panorama apresentado pelos engenheiros, vale checar quais são as recomendações da fabricante, pois as orientações podem variar conforme a marca e o modelo do aparelho.

Em seu site, a Lenovo afirma que “manter a bateria conectada por longos períodos não fará com que ela seja sobrecarregada”.

Mas faz um alerta: “Se a bateria permanecer carregada em ou próximo a 100%, a Lenovo recomenda configurar o recurso Battery Charge Threshold para limitar a carga.”

Segundo a marca, isso minimiza a degradação desnecessária . A Lenovo ainda recomenda definir o limite superior de carga para 80% ou menos.

A Dell segue na mesma linha, afirmando que não há problema em manter o aparelho na tomada, mas com algumas precauções.

“É uma boa prática desconectar o notebook da tomada de vez em quando para permitir que a bateria passe por ciclos de descarga e recarga, o que também pode ajudar a manter a saúde da bateria”, comentou a fabricante, em nota.

Já a HP aconselha contra o uso do dispositivo na tomada por longos períodos. Segundo a marca, isso pode fazer com que a bateria perca sua calibração e capacidade de carregar corretamente.

A HP orienta que o usuário deixe a bateria do notebook descarregar completamente de tempos em tempos e, em seguida, volte a carregá-la totalmente, para ajudar a mantê-la calibrada.

💡 Dicas práticas para preservar a vida útil da bateria do notebook

Segundo Bruno Lima, um dos maiores responsáveis de danos à bateria do notebook é o impacto físico, causado por quedas ou batidas.

“Não pode ter impacto de forma alguma . A bateria, na verdade, é um conjunto de metais com um eletrólito, onde acontece uma reação química que gera energia”, explica Lima.

“Se você derruba, acaba danificando essa estrutura; elas acabam se aproximando, rolando ou rompendo e perdem a capacidade de carga”, completa.

Lima também aponta que temperaturas extremas podem afetar a bateria de forma parecida com o impacto físico, já que a dilatação pelo calor ou a retração pelo frio causam movimento dos componentes.

Já Ciuccio avisa que é preciso tomar cuidado com a adequação do carregador . Pegar um carregador emprestado, especialmente quando é de outra marca, pode fazer mal à saúde da bateria, mesmo que tenha a mesma entrada.

Portanto, não é recomendável usar carregadores que não sejam originais e feitos para o seu produto.

"Tem um problema de interface de tensão, que pode fazer a sua bateria sofrer um pouquinho", comentou Ciuccio. " E se o cabo estiver torcido, danificado, pode até ter fuga da corrente e você não conseguir carregar a bateria. "

Os engenheiros dão algumas dicas de como cuidar da bateria e prolongar sua vida útil:

Evite deixar o notebook no sol ou apoiar sobre a cama, para não esquentar.

Evite descarregar o notebook por completo muitas vezes.

Se a bateria zerou, deixe carregar até 100% antes de tirar da tomada.

Os primeiros sinais de que a bateria está no fim da vida útil incluem o estufamento – quando ela fica visivelmente inchada – e a perda de velocidade no carregamento.

Veja a seguir modelos de notebooks de R$ 3.700 a R$ 9.900, consultados em setembro, nas principais lojas da internet.

articles.title: The investigation into Tesla Autopilot’s emergency vehicle problem is getting bigger
articles.summary: The investigation into Tesla Autopilot is now affecting the automaker’s rivals. NHTSA sent requests to 12 major car companies, including Ford, GM, VW, and Toyota, requesting information into their Level 2 driver assist systems.
articles.body: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is requesting advanced driver assist data from 12 automakers as it seeks to expand its investigation into Tesla’s Autopilot. The government is probing a dozen incidents involving Teslas crashing into emergency vehicles. According to Automotive News, the agency’s Office of Defects Investigation sent letters to a dozen major automakers, including Ford, General Motors, Toyota, and Volkswagen, requesting information regarding their Level 2 driver assist systems, in which the vehicle can simultaneously control steering, braking, and acceleration under specific circumstances. Automakers are being asked to provide the number of vehicles with Level 2 systems that have been manufactured in the US, as well as the total number of miles covered with those systems engaged and a recent list of any changes or updates. NHTSA is also requesting customer complaints, field and crash reports, and any lawsuits related to the Level 2 systems. The data request comes less than two weeks after NHTSA sent an order to Tesla to provide data on the operation of its Autopilot system, including details on which of its sold vehicles are equipped with Autopilot as well as the system’s operating parameters. The agency’s investigation into Tesla could have wide-ranging implications for Tesla, which has pushed the boundaries in releasing experimental software to untrained customers in order to advance its vision of autonomous driving. NHTSA’s investigation covers an estimated 765,000 Tesla vehicles that were released from 2014 through 2021. The agency is looking into 12 crashes in which Tesla owners using the company’s Autopilot features have crashed into stationary emergency vehicles, resulting in 17 injuries and one fatality. Most of these incidents took place after dark, with the software ignoring scene control measures including warning lights, flares, cones, and an illuminated arrow board. Tesla has until October 22nd to hand over the data. US-based automakers like Ford, GM, and Stellantis have until November 3rd, and all other car companies, like Toyota, Subaru, Nissan, and Honda, have until November 17th. Automakers that fail to respond could face civil penalties of up to $115 million. A spokesperson for Toyota said the company would comply with NHTSA’s request. A VW spokesperson declined comment, while media contacts for the other automakers did not respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: The original smart oven goes dark.
articles.summary:
Today, Weber shut down June Oven’s cloud servers, leaving ovens that cost up to $1,500 unable to do anything beyond basic functions.
Owners were notified in July that September 22 would be the end, cutting off remote control via the app, live camera viewing, AI food recognition, and software updates. The ovens still work through their built-in touchscreens, including local food recognition, but support for repairs and parts is also done.
Weber bought June in 2021 and quickly discontinued the ovens, folding June’s technology into Weber Connect. It says it won’t open-source the app because the IP is used in current and potentially future products.
[Link: What is happening to the June App? | https://consumer-care.weber.com/s/article/What-is-happening-to-the-June-App?language=en_US | Weber]

articles.title: Boat launches smart earbuds range with Crest AI; offers Airdopes Prime 800 D, Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Nirvana Ion ANC earbuds
articles.summary: Audio News: Boat has launched its first smart audio devices range featuring Boat Crest AI, its AI-powered platform built with Google Gemini. The lineup includes B.
articles.body: Boat has launched its first smart audio devices range featuring Boat Crest AI, its AI-powered platform built with Google Gemini. The lineup includes Boat Airdopes Prime 800, Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC. With the launch, Boat is introducing a new proposition for personal audio — ‘Intelligent Ears’ — earbuds designed not just for listening, but to listen, understand, converse and assist.In a press release, the company said that the Crest AI is built around a simpler idea: bringing intelligence to something consumers already wear throughout their day — their earbuds. At the heart of the experience are three capabilities — Crest Ask, G- Assist and Crest Translate, or simply: Ask. Assist. Translate.With Crest Ask, users can ask questions, explore ideas, learn and have natural conversations with AI. Instead of repeatedly reaching for a phone or typing a query, users can ask follow-up questions and continue the conversation through their earbuds.With G- Assist take the experience from conversation to action. With integration across Google Gmail, Tasks, and Calendar, users can access everyday productivity and communication capabilities through voice. From asking the assistant to “summarize my day” to “reply to an email,” G-Assist helps users manage tasks, stay on top of schedules, and interact with their digital routines without reaching for their phones.Crest Translate enables real-time, two-way translation across 25+ languages, helping people speaking different languages communicate more naturally.Gaurav Nayyar, CEO, Boat said “Why should intelligence be limited to our rooms, desks, pockets or screens? We believe it can become much more natural and simply be with you. With Crest AI, built with Google Gemini, we are bringing that intelligence to your ears. Our idea of ‘Intelligent Ears’ is simple: earbuds that can listen, understand, converse and assist. But this is just the beginning, we are working on multiple other use cases. For ten years, Boat has helped India listen. Now, we want to help India listen, understand, converse and assist”.The Boat Airdopes Prime 800 D combines Crest AI capabilities with Dolby Audio and 11mm dynamic drivers tuned to Boat Signature Sound. The earbuds offer up to 45 hours of total playback, Multipoint Connectivity and four microphones with AI-ENx technology, bringing together entertainment, communication and intelligent assistance in one device.Crest AI is also available on the Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC. The Boat Airdopes Prime 800 D, Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC are available through the Boat website and leading e-commerce platforms.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Simon Cowell to miss America’s Got Talent Season 21 finale amid health concerns; KSI to replace him on judges’ panel
articles.summary: Simon Cowell will not be part of the America’s Got Talent Season 21 finale as he continues to recover from a medical procedure for his ongoing back pr.
articles.body: Simon Cowell will not be part of the America’s Got Talent Season 21 finale as he continues to recover from a medical procedure for his ongoing back problems. The veteran judge and creator of the NBC talent show had been away from the live episodes in recent weeks and was initially hoped to return before the season came to an end.However, Simon will now remain absent for both parts of the finale, which are scheduled to air on September 22 and September 23. His absence means viewers will see a different face occupying his usual spot on the judges’ panel as the remaining contestants compete for the Season 21 title.YouTuber, musician and boxer KSI has been chosen to join the panel for the finale. He will sit alongside Howie Mandel, Sofia Vergara and Mel B during the final performances as well as the results episode. KSI is not new to the Got Talent franchise. He previously appeared as a judge on Britain’s Got Talent, giving him experience with the format and its high-pressure auditions.Simon stepped away from America’s Got Talent in August while dealing with his back-related health issues. Following his procedure, fellow judge Howie Mandel had shared an encouraging update, saying he had been told that the treatment had gone well and that Simon was doing okay.Earlier, Howie had also expressed hope that Simon would recover in time to return for the moment when the new winner of the competition was announced.While Simon has been away, the show has continued with a series of guest judges filling in at different stages. Among those who have joined the panel are actor and comedian Kenan Thompson and former America’s Got Talent judge Heidi Klum.The Season 21 performance finale is scheduled for September 22 at 8 p.m. ET on NBC, with the results episode following on September 23 at 9 p.m. ET.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. articles.title: An endurance watch with solar on both sides.
articles.summary:
Des Yap did some initial testing of the new $649.99 T-Rex Dual Solar from Amazfit — the first endurance watch with a bright and colorful OLED to be fitted with teeny-weeny solar panels. The ring around the display can extend life a bit, but the larger rear panel around the heart-rate sensor can add a few percentage points of charge when you arrive at camp, or when the watch is slung off a running vest, so maybe you can leave your ultralight power bank home on your next multi-day adventure.

articles.title: Motorola showcases Signature 27 with 50MP main camera and 200MP periscope telephoto camera
articles.summary: Tech News News: Motorola has showcased the Signature 27, its second smartphone in the Signature series and one of the first phones announced with Qualcomm’s latest Sn.
articles.body: Motorola has showcased the Signature 27, its second smartphone in the Signature series and one of the first phones announced with Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. The smartphone was unveiled at the Snapdragon Summit 2026 on Tuesday and comes with a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera and a 200MP periscope telephoto camera. Motorola is also changing its naming system with this phone, using the final two digits of the upcoming year for its new generations. The company has not yet announced the price or exact sale date, but says the Signature 27 will launch globally later this year.Motorola Signature 27 featuresThe Motorola Signature 27 is powered by Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor. Motorola says the chipset brings improvements to on-device AI, camera performance, gaming response and download speeds. The phone also comes with Motorola’s ArcticMesh cooling system. It combines diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal and copper mesh with a redesigned 3D vapour chamber. Motorola says the new vapour chamber is 40% larger than the previous generation.Motorola Signature 27 gets a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera along with a 200MP periscope telephoto camera. Motorola has also introduced its Video Enhancement Engine, which uses AI to study a scene before and during video recording and adjust colour tones in real time.The phone will also support Google's Gemini Omni, which can use prompts, photos or existing video clips to create a finished video. Google's Lyria can be used to generate music and soundtracks.The phone will be available in Pantone Coal Smoke and Pantone Capulet Green. The Coal Smoke version has a woven texture designed to improve grip and durability, while Capulet Green gets a brushed, textile-inspired finish.Motorola Signature 27 operating systemMotorola says the Signature 27 will receive seven years of OS upgrades and is expected to launch with Android 17. It is also the company's first smartphone with Audio by B&O, with the branding etched onto the rear panel.Motorola has not yet revealed the phone's display, battery capacity, charging speed, RAM, storage or other camera sensors. Pricing and the exact launch date are also yet to be announced.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Xiaomi’s new 18 Pro phones improve on Samsung’s privacy display
articles.summary: An international launch for the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max is confirmed for later this year.
articles.body: Xiaomi’s new 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max launched in China today, and feature a more flexible take on the privacy display tech introduced this year on Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra. They combine it with returning rear screens, two 200-megapixel cameras, and both of Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chips. A global launch is confirmed for later this year — especially welcome since last year’s 17 Pro phones skipped international markets. The two 18 Pro phones look similar to the 17 Pros, with similar compact displays built around the rear cameras, capable of displaying notifications, taking selfies, playing simple games, and more. The bigger changes are to the front screen, which is now equipped with hardware-level privacy features much like the S26 Ultra’s. Xiaomi’s implementation looks smarter than Samsung’s though: when you activate it for a specific app, it will not only turn on when that app is opened, but apply to notifications, floating windows, and split-screen views, without affecting the rest of the display. Location-based triggers allow you to set it to turn on when you reach work, or off when you come home, with smart triggers for when it detects locations like airports or elevators. It can also use the selfie camera to detect prying eyes and suggest activating the privacy mode. [Image: [Image: [Image: The two phones differ in size, with a 6.4-inch display on the Pro and 6.9 inches for the Pro Max. Battery varies accordingly: 7,000mAh or 8,500mAh respectively, using a high 32 percent silicon content. The other difference between the two is the chipset, with the Snapdragon 8 Gen 6 Elite in the Pro and the Extreme version in the Pro Max, though differences between the two chips are slight. Cameras are led by a 200-megapixel main camera using a large 1/1.28-inch-type sensor (the Light Fusion 960 in the Pro, and 960L in the Pro Max, though they seem similar). A 200-megapixel, 75mm telephoto joins it, the same on both phones, using Samsung’s 1/1.56-inch HP5 sensor and with a minimum focus distance of 12cm. A 50-megapixel ultrawide completes the trio. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Xiaomi’s launch follows similar announcements this week for the Vivo X500 and Oppo Find X10 flagships. The two 18 Pro phones start from ¥5,999 (about $900), and join the 18 Fold in Xiaomi’s new flagship lineup, but we’re still waiting for the regular Xiaomi 18 and the 18 Ultra, likely to appear next spring. An international launch for at least one 18 Pro phone will come later this year, though we’re still waiting to hear if the Fold will ever leave China.

articles.title: FCC chair blasts House Democrats 'extreme position' on gender ideology in kids' programming in fiery letter
articles.summary: FCC Chairman Brendan Carr fired back at House Democrats who opposed the agency's push to reform children's TV ratings over content pushing gender ideology.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX — The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr on Tuesday issued a fiery response to the opposition from House Democrats over the agency's effort to reform television ratings for children's programming, some of which promotes gender ideology. In April, the FCC issued a public notice seeking feedback about parents' concern about the content of shows their children watch, suggesting the current ratings system is outdated and deems "shows with transgender and gender non-binary programming as appropriate for children and young children" and that new ratings may be necessary. That prompted a response in June from Democrats on the Congressional Equality Caucus, who accused the FCC of wanting to "censor the inclusion of transgender characters or topics" from children's programming and said that the current ratings system is "satisfactory and overwhelmingly popular among parents." WASHINGTON FATHER SUES SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR DENYING RELIGIOUS OPT-OUT FOR 5TH GRADER FROM LGBTQ INSTRUCTION "We strongly believe that parents should decide what their children watch on television," the lawmakers wrote. "Programs should not have higher ratings or content warning simply because of the identity of the programs’ characters. Applying higher ratings or content warnings because of a character’s gender identity would be harmful to transgender people and transgender acceptance and would harken back to a time when politicians sought to censor television programming because they included minorities." The House Democrats continued, "Any attempt by FCC to censor content because it includes transgender characters or topics would raise both legal and constitutional concerns... Any attempt to issue rating warnings for depictions and themes related to transgender people would also raise concerns of content-based and viewpoint discrimination in violation of the First Amendment." BLUE STATE SCHOOL DISTRICT ACCUSED OF DEFYING SUPREME COURT, HIDING GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS In a letter sent Tuesday to Congressional Equality Caucus Chair Rep. Mark Takano, D-Calif., Carr expressed regret for the stance the Democratic lawmakers had taken. "I am deeply concerned by the position that you and over 60 of your Democrat colleagues in the House of Representatives are taking regarding the right of parents to know whether their sons or daughters are being exposed to controversial gender identity ideologies—including the promotion of transgender and gender non-binary programming—in television shows that are rated as appropriate for young children," Carr began the letter obtained by Fox News Digital. "In your letter, you come out swinging against both transparency and common sense," Carr added. "You stake out the radical position that parents have no right to know whether controversial gender identity ideologies are being promoted in children’s television programming. In your view, parents should not be empowered to make informed choices about the programs their children watch." Carr called the Democrats' defense of transgender people an "extreme position" which he said comes as children's programming is "secretly promoting gender ideology to young kids without the knowledge or consent of their parents." He went on to list several examples of gender ideology appearing in children's programming, citing an episode of Disney Jr.'s "Muppet Babies" reboot (TV-Y) where Gonzo wants to dress as a princess instead of a knight, calls himself "Gonzo-rella" and is referred to in the episode with the "they" pronoun, as well as a trans character in Netflix's "Strawberry Shortcake: Berry in the Big City" (TV-Y) and pansexual and non-binary characters in the Disney Channel's animated series "Primos" (TV-Y7). "Keeping parents in the dark about the nature of these programs is a feature not a bug of the effort. Indeed, you write in your letter that 'many recognize their gender identity at a young age.' And you appear to suggest that informing parents would prevent 'self-acceptance,'" Carr wrote. "Recent studies show a massive spike in younger people identifying as transgender with some attributing this to media exposure. But your position that New York and Hollywood programmers should have a direct line to children without parental knowledge is at total odds with the law Congress passed." "Opposing transparency puts you on the wrong side of the issue. Parents are nearly unanimous in wanting to know what their children are watching and to determine for their own families what shows are appropriate. Despite your opposition, the FCC will continue its work to empower parents and continue to engage with stakeholders as part of the agency’s open and ongoing proceeding," Carr added. articles.title: LinkedIn is cracking down on fake employees.
articles.summary:
The platform is testing a way for users to verify their profile by getting people they’ve actually worked or studied with (who are already verified) to vouch for them. LinkedIn is also testing a feature for company pages that forces users claiming current employment to verify themselves, and companies can now instantly remove fake employees from search results.

articles.title: Motivational quote of the day by Simon Cowell: ‘Failures aren’t great to go through, but you learn from them,’ a powerful life lesson on how setbacks are not stopping points but stepping stones
articles.summary: Failure is never an option for most people, as it can lead to disappointment, frustration and the feeling of having tried your hardest and it still not
articles.body: Failure is never an option for most people, as it can lead to disappointment, frustration and the feeling of having tried your hardest and it still not being enough. However, one of Simon Cowell’s quotes serves as a gentle reminder that even the shiniest successes and the most anticipated events can tarnish with time. The only way to avoid this is to embrace failure as part of the learning process.Motivational quote of the day by Simon Cowell: ‘Failures aren’t great to go through, but you learn from them.’What is the meaning of the quote of Simon Cowell?The quote by Simon Cowell, “Failures aren’t great to go through but you learn from them,” signifies that although failures could be dreadful experiences, individuals can always learn from them. From the quotation, one can understand that rather than giving up on a task, one should question the reasons for failing and use the insight to do things right in the future.Why is the quote of Simon Cowell relevant today?The saying is relevant because, to this day, people experience failures in various aspects of life. Failure could be in career, academics, relationships, business, or even art. Whenever one faces a challenge, it could be disheartening and disappointing to think that the efforts put into a venture could have been futile. Nonetheless, Cowell’s quote provides a different perspective on failures because when one is unsuccessful in certain undertakings, it does not imply that they will never be successful. Therefore, one should reflect on their failures and use the insights to be more careful in the future endeavors. The quotation is also significant to the contemporary society because individuals like Cowell are more interested in the outcomes of their actions.Early life of Simon CowellSimon Phillip Cowell was born on October 7, 1959, in London, England, and he was raised in Elstree, Hertfordshire. His father was Eric Cowell, a music business executive and property developer, while his mother was Julie Cowell, a former ballet dancer and socialite. Cowell attended Dover College before leaving school at sixteen.After leaving school, Cowell worked several jobs before entering the music industry. His father helped him get a job in the mailroom at EMI Music Publishing. He eventually moved into A&R, where he began developing his experience in identifying and working with musical talent.His early career also included setbacks. Cowell went on to form Fanfare Records, which initially found success but eventually collapsed in 1989. The setback left him in financial difficulty and he moved back in with his family. He later returned to the music business as a consultant for BMG and gradually rebuilt his career.Simon Cowell’s rise to fameHis major television breakthrough came with Pop Idol in 2001. The show’s success was followed by American Idol, which premiered in the US in 2002, where Cowell became known for his direct judging style. He later became associated with major talent franchises including The X Factor and America’s Got Talent.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Eight Sleep's new Pod 6 comes in smaller and solo sizes, starting at $1,999 | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Eight Sleep said the new pod is 20% faster than the previous generation.
articles.body:
Sleep tech company Eight Sleep on Wednesday launched its new Pod 6 device in a smaller size than previous editions to fit more bed frames, along with solo sizes for one-person use. The company said that the device can be used to adjust the temperature on either side 20% faster than the previous-generation gadget.

Because the new pod has a 50% smaller footprint, it can fit most bed frames. The company claims the device has 9x more sensors, enabling it to understand granular temperature controls for each user even if they are sleeping close together. Plus, it can ignore data from a pet or a kid sleeping on the bed with two users.

The Pod 6 is available starting today in over 37 countries, starting at $1,999 for solo sizes and $2,699 for standard sizes. Solo sizes can fit a twin bed and one side of queen, king, and California King beds. Standard sizes will be available in queen, king, and California King. Plus, it can work with existing add-ons like a blanket, pillow cover, and base.

Beyond new sleep products, the company is pursuing Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval to transition its Eight Sleep Pod into a regulated medical device for sleep apnea in the U.S.

Earlier this year, the company raised $50 million from Tether at a $1.5 billion valuation . Eight Sleep also took steps to expand its international footprint by launching its product in China, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Singapore in the last year, with China becoming one of the fastest-growing regions.

The company’s CEO Matteo Franceschetti told TechCrunch that international markets contribute over 30% of revenue. He mentioned that the sleep tech company plans to expand into other regions of Asia and Latin America. Franceschetti noted that the company is keeping a keen eye on the component crunch in the electronics sector, but didn’t say whether it will impact pricing.

“We definitely see the market changing a little bit because AI companies are requesting a lot of different components. We are adjusting our supply chain [to counter that]. It’s definitely something that we need to watch out for, particularly as our devices become more and more, I would say, compute-heavy and intelligent to be able to provide AI features to our users,” he said.

articles.title: This $199 GPS sports watch is repairable, modular, and open-source
articles.summary: The $199 Una Watch says it’s the first GPS fitness smartwatch that’s modular and repairable, with open-source hardware and software.
articles.body: The Una Watch costs less than most Garmin watches now that its price has been lowered from the Kickstarter offer of $350 to $199, but its modular, repairable design grabbed my attention first. It features a 1.2-inch MIP LCD display and up to 10 days of battery life, similar to the Garmin Forerunner 70 or the Pebble Round 2 I preordered earlier this year. Like Pebble’s revamped watches, the Una Watch is also open-source, including its SDK, housing, and circuit boards, but it has more fitness features out of the box than Pebble’s watches currently offer. Una is also encouraging users to build their own apps for it, including with vibe coding — it says users can “ask an AI coding assistant to interpret Una’s developer documentation, produce code, diagnose errors and refine the resulting application.” Una says every component in the watch is “accessible with a standard tool,” so users can repair or upgrade it themselves. The open-source mechanical components also open the door for users to design and 3D print their own accessories or mods for it, like converting it into a cycling computer. It features dual-frequency GPS, 24/7 heart rate tracking, a barometric altimeter, a six-axis accelerometer and gyroscope, a three-axis magnetometer and a replaceable 280mAh battery with USB-C charging. However, the Una Watch is only IPX5 splash- and showerproof, not fully waterproof.

articles.title: One of the best Metroid games for the Switch is 30 percent off
articles.summary: Metroid Prime Remastered is available digitally for about $28. You can also save $50 on Apple’s full-size Magic Keyboard, and more.
articles.body: Nintendo’s “Customer Appreciation” sale continues through September 26th. It includes discounts on Switch games and accessories, and I thought I’d call out one of my favorite games that’s cheaper than ever. Metroid Prime Remastered is down to $27.99 in digital format for the Switch and Switch 2, and it’s among the best remasters I’ve played because it makes smart improvements to an already-great game. You can get it for this price at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart. The physical version costs around $42 at those retailers. [Product: Metroid Prime Remastered | Most Metroid fans have already played this one — maybe multiple times, even — but if you’ve somehow missed out, here’s your sign to pick it up. It applies a modern coat of updated textures and improved lighting to the 2002 GameCube title, and it runs at a smooth frame rate. Notably, the control scheme doesn’t require motion controls like the Wii re-release did. For about the same price as this digital title, true fans can also buy the Metroid Prime 1-3: A Visual Retrospective hardcover book. Normally $49.99, it’s $28.50 at Amazon and Walmart for the 208-page art book covering the original trilogy, peppered with some fantastic quotes from people who worked on the games. It’s an unusually candid look into Nintendo’s first-person shooter series and the company’s game design philosophy. It’d make for a great holiday gift. Read our coverage of the book. Other great Verge-approved deals * Flow is one of the best animated movies of the past few years, and now it’s cheaper than ever to own a digital copy. Unless you have HBO Max to watch it on demand, snag the 4K version from Apple TV or Amazon for $4.99. The voiceless tale follows a cat who survives a huge flood that leaves civilizations in ruin. The perilous (yet adorable) adventure sees the cat relying on other animals to survive. It’s just a fantastic way to spend 90 minutes. * It’s never a bad time to recommend a cable as useful as Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable. The two-headed cable can charge two devices from a single charging port (up to 140W for a single device), and the six-foot version is down to $15.99 at Amazon. This is only $4 off, and it’s far from the first time we’ve seen this deal. But it’s never been cheaper, and it’s practical cable that will likely improve your charging setup. My wife and I use it to cycle between charging our MacBooks and an iPad, occasionally throwing a phone or Kindle into the mix. * Best Buy is trolling us a bit with today’s price on the white Magic Keyboard with Touch ID. We focused yesterday on the $30 discount for the black version of the wireless keyboard that brought it down to $169.99. That deal is gone, but the model with white key caps is down to $149.99 at Best Buy. It’s compatible with all Macs that have Apple silicon, dating back to the M1 models (so long as you have macOS 15.1 or later). It recharges via USB-C, and has a full numerical pad, plus other keys for easier navigation on your computer.

articles.title: Logitech’s new Blue Yeti 2 mic adjusts itself to where you are
articles.summary: Logitech G’s Blue Yeti 2 USB microphone builds on its predecessor’s classic design with some modern upgrades.
articles.body: The original Blue Yeti has been one of the most recognizable go-to USB microphones for content creators since it launched in 2009, and now it finally has a successor. Launching today under Logitech G, the Blue Yeti 2 adds some modern upgrades, including an interactive LED display, AI de-noising, and a proximity based voice sensor — which resolves a notable flaw with its predecessor’s design while still paying homage to it. It’s available in black or white color options for $159.99, which is comparatively cheaper than Shure’s popular MV7 series USB microphones, which are the current choice for podcasters and start at $299. It’s also interestingly just $10 more than the original Blue Yeti’s launch price 17 years ago. A lot has happened since then, with Logitech acquiring the Blue audio production company for $117 million in 2018 and later killing the Blue brand entirely in 2023 when it merged the products with its own gaming-focused Logitech G sub brand. That means this new launch should just be called the Yeti 2, but Logitech clearly has some nostalgia to play with here. [Image: If you prefer to manually adjust your gain and other audio settings then this image suggests you can do so. The Blue Yeti 2 includes a built-in audio proximity sensor that tracks your voice in 3D, and automatically adjusts gain, EQ, and pickup patterns to preserve recording quality regardless of how close or far you are when moving around the mic. That should make this a more beginner friendly USB microphone than the original, as you don’t need to have any knowledge or experience with manually tweaking those settings to achieve optimal results. Plus, it still retains a similar design to the OG Yeti which confused people into incorrectly speaking into the top of it, an issue this new sensor should address. [Image: [Image: It provides up to 24-bit / 48 kHz high-resolution capture. Other audio features include integrated direct digital signal processing (DSP) to improve voice clarity without additional software, and AI-powered noise removal to reduce unwanted background sounds like computer fans and mouse clicks. Given Logitech is pitching this to streamers, the 1.3-inch color LED display on the front where the controls are located also features a “Yeti character” that provides visual feedback on gain levels and polar patterns.

articles.title: She'd rather work for Rupert Murdoch than stay at CNN. Here's why
articles.summary: Bay Area tech journalist and podcaster Kara Swisher says she plans to leave CNN rather than work under David Ellison once the merger between Paramount and Wa...
articles.body:
Kara Swisher has reached a breaking point with one of the biggest media deals of the year.

The Bay Area tech journalist and podcaster says she plans to leave CNN rather than work under David Ellison once the merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery is complete.

Ellison is CEO of Paramount Skydance, which has been cleared to merge with Warner Bros. Discovery after reaching a deal with California Attorney General Rob Bonta that was announced Monday, Sept. 21.

"I'd rather work for Rupert Murdoch," Swisher, referring to the controversial media mogul who owns Fox News, told author and academic Scott Galloway on her "Pivot" podcast.

Swisher went on to call Ellison and his father, Oracle CEO Larry Ellison , "terrible media owners" and said she's already asked her agent if could get out of her contract with the cable news network earlier. The agreement runs through the end of the year.

"It's only a few months, right?" Swisher said on the podcast episode that dropped Tuesday, Sept. 22. "I just can't. I was trying to figure out ways I could work with them in some like licensing way. But then I thought, 'F- these guys.' I don't want to work for them. I just don't."

Bonta had been leading a 12-state coalition that included 11 other attorneys general in a lawsuit that was intended to block the $111 billion merger, but has agreed to drop the lawsuit after Ellison agreed to certain concessions intended to preserve film and television production schedules.

Ellison is working to complete the merger by Oct. 1. The deal would combine Paramount's holdings - including Paramount Pictures, CBS, Showtime and the Paramount+ streaming service - with Warner Bros. Discovery's entities such as Warner Bros. Pictures, HBO, CNN and the streaming service HBO Max.

Many observers note that CNN may drastically change if Ellison places controversial CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss in charge of the 46-year-old network founded by Ted Turner as the first 24-hour news channel.

"They've been very nicely trying to keep me, and I have a lot of regard for the executives there now," Swisher said. "But I am not staying. I have other things that make more money, that matter more, that have a bigger audience."

Swisher and Galloway are scheduled to bring a live version of the "Pivot" podcast to the Golden Gate Theatre in San Francisco on Nov. 7.

articles.title: Microsoft’s new Surface Mouse has haptic feedback and a customizable action button
articles.summary: The $79.99 Surface Mouse will start shipping on October 13th.
articles.body: Microsoft is launching a second generation of its Surface Mouse next month that includes haptic feedback support. The Surface Mouse also has a customizable action button for the first time, which is primarily designed for quick access to Copilot (of course), but can be configured to work with other shortcuts from the Surface app. “Its haptic feedback adds a small, purposeful physical response to the moment you usually only see on a screen: a click registering, a window snapping into place or an object aligning just right,” says Brett Ostrum, corporate vice president of Surface Devices. “It is subtle by design, but noticeable within seconds — and hard to give up once you have it.” The haptic feedback works with things like clicks, drags, and alignment throughout Windows 11, but the tactile feedback also triggers in apps like PowerPoint, Affinity, Concepts, and Filmora. Microsoft added support for haptic feedback in Windows 11 earlier this year, and so far it’s mainly Microsoft and Logitech that are supporting it with dedicated hardware. Logitech’s MX Master 4 has haptic feedback, and its Pro X2 Superstrike (and today’s new X3) includes a haptic-based clicks system that doesn’t support the Windows 11 haptic feedback. The upcoming Surface Laptop Ultra also has a haptic trackpad. After originally launching the Surface Mouse in 2016 and not updating it since, Microsoft has now redesigned it to be more comfortable for all-day use, with a soft-touch material at the top. Thanks to Bluetooth 6.0 support, you can now also pair it with up to three devices. The new Surface Mouse will be available on October 13th, the same day Microsoft launches its refreshed Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch devices. It will be priced at $79.99, and available in black and platinum color options.

articles.title: Microsoft refreshes its smaller Surface Pro and Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus
articles.summary: Microsoft is refreshing its Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch. The hardware remains the same, but the chips get upgraded to Qualcomm’s X2 Plus.
articles.body: Microsoft is refreshing its Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch devices with Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon X2 Plus chips. The smaller Surface devices retain the same design and hardware features from last year, with faster and more capable chips inside and higher price tags (thanks RAMageddon!). While the 12-inch Surface Pro started at $799.99 last year, it’s debuting on October 13th at a starting price of $1,149.99. Likewise, the 13-inch Surface Laptop was originally priced at $899.99, but it’s up to $1,199.99 this time around. There’s no base 8GB model this time, causing some of the price increase, as both devices launch with a minimum of 16GB of RAM and can be configured up to 24GB. Pricing aside, Microsoft is promising that the six-core Snapdragon X2 Plus chips will deliver up to 18 percent more efficient battery performance, more than 60 percent faster graphics performance, and up to 95 percent faster local AI inferencing on the built-in NPU. [Image: That’s a lot of percentages, but what it equates to on these devices is better battery life and improved performance. On the Surface Pro 12-inch Second Edition, as Microsoft calls it, that means an extra hour of web browsing (up to 13 hours in total), and on the Surface Laptop 13-inch Second Edition it’s two extra hours of web browsing usage (up to 18 hours in total). Microsoft is using similar displays on these models as last year, so the Surface Pro 12-inch has a 2196 x 1464 (220 PPI) LCD display that runs at up to 90Hz. The Surface Laptop 13-inch still ships with a 1920 x 1280 (178 PPI) display that only runs at 60Hz. Both displays have been upgraded from 400 nits of brightness to 500 nits, though. Port selection remains the same, too. Both devices include two USB-C 3.2 ports, and the Surface Laptop 13-inch also has a USB-A 3.2 port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. Both also support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity. I’m surprised that Microsoft hasn’t upgraded at least one of these smaller Surface devices with a haptic trackpad, particularly because Windows 11 now adds subtle haptic nudges, and the Surface Laptop Ultra ships with haptic feedback. Microsoft is launching a second edition of its Surface Mouse with integrated haptics, and you can read all about that here. Microsoft is also bringing back the black color option for both of these smaller Surface devices, with platinum silver or violet colors available too. Both devices will also be sold to commercial customers, and the Surface Pro 12-inch will be available in an optional 5G configuration.

articles.title: Jeff Garlin Says ‘Undiagnosed Bipolar’ Made Him ‘Mean’ on ‘The Goldbergs’ Set; Wendi McLendon-Covey Responds: ‘I Remember Things Differently’
articles.summary: Jeff Garlin revealed in a recent interview on The Daily Beast’s “Obsessed” podcast (via Entertainment Weekly) that he had undiagnosed bipolar disorder during...
articles.body:
Jeff Garlin revealed in a recent interview on The Daily Beast's "Obsessed" podcast (via Entertainment Weekly ) that he had undiagnosed bipolar disorder during the making of ABC's "The Goldbergs," which he notably exited from after an HR investigation into multiple claims of inappropriate conduct against him. The 1980s-set family sitcom, which ran for 10 seasons and 229 episodes from 2013 to 2023, starred Garlin opposite Wendi McLendon-Covey. Garlin exited in 2021.

"At the time, I was undiagnosed bipolar," Garlin said on the podcast, noting he got his diagnosis after exiting the series. "I was miserable on the show, and I was miserable with my performance. And [Wendi] was always trying to tell me, 'Hey, you're really great on the show.' I didn't believe her. I just got to the point where I had to quit, and she was very resentful."

Garlin added, "Being bipolar, I was either one of three things: dark, dark, dark, dark, didn't talk and look at anyone; happy to the point of mania, never turning off my thing; or mean — really, really mean."

McLendon-Covey reacted to Garlin's comments on Instagram by disputing his comments: "Huh. Let's just say I remember things very differently, as does the crew, the other actors, the writers, and our executives."

When Garlin exited "The Goldbergs" in 2021, two sources close to the production confirmed to Variety that it was a mutual decision between the actor and the network. Shortly before, Garlin addressed allegations against him in an interview with Vanity Fair , acknowledging that an HR investigation into his on-set behavior had been ongoing for the past three years and dismissing a rumor that he had been fired from the series.

"We have a difference of opinion, Sony and myself. Okay. My opinion is, I have my process about how I'm funny, in terms of the scene and what I have to do. They feel that it makes for a quote 'unsafe' workspace," Garlin said at the time. "Now, mind you, my silliness making an unsafe workspace — I don't understand how that is… I am always a kind and thoughtful person. I make mistakes, sure. But my comedy is about easing people's pain. Why would I ever want to cause pain in anybody for a laugh? That's bullying. That's just uncalled for."

The allegations against Garlin ranged from unwanted hugging and touching people on set to telling jokes that made others uncomfortable. McLendon-Covey later said during an interview with Andy Cohen for SiriusXM that Garlin's exit was "a long time coming."

"That it finally happened, it was like, 'Ok, finally someone is listening to us.' But that was kind of hard though because we had lost George Segal in real life," she added. "To have to go through another loss on a sitcom…you can't keep asking your audience to mourn people. That's not why they tune in… I'm exhausted by that topic and the PTSD of it all. I just feel like the less people know about that, the better. No one benefits from knowing anything."

"The Goldbergs" was in the middle of filming its ninth season when Garlin was fired. As Variety exclusively reported at the time, producers decided to keep Garlin's character on the show for the rest of the season by using off-camera dialogue and unused takes pulled from earlier episodes, as well as previously shot images of Garlin. The actor's stand-in was also used in group scenes, but he was shot from the back. The final result was visually awkward and earned so many complaints on social media that McLendon-Covey even weighed in at the time.

"This season threw us for a loop because it's hard to incorporate someone who doesn't want to be there and wants to leave mid-scene, and we weren't about to rewrite the second half of the season," the comedian wrote on Twitter at the time . "We're doing our best."

When "The Goldbergs" kicked off its 10th and final season last fall, the show killed off Garlin's character.

articles.title: Qualcomm will finally support Linux on Snapdragon X2 chips.
articles.summary:
“For many years developers have asked us for one thing, Linux on Snapdragon. We heard you,” says Kedar Kondap, SVP and general manager of compute and gaming at Qualcomm. Speaking at Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Summit, Kondap says Linux support with Debian will be available “at the end of this year” for Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon X2 series of chips. articles.title: Meta Connect 2026 live blog: On the ground at Mark Zuckerberg’s next big product launch
articles.summary: The Verge is on the ground at Meta’s Connect keynote, which will feature CEO Mark Zuckerberg. Follow along with our coverage live.
articles.body: It’s time once again for Meta’s annual September product launch event, and The Verge is on the ground in Menlo Park to cover the show live. Meta says that today’s keynote by Mark Zuckerberg will be about how “Meta is building a future for everyone” — something he wrote at length about in a recent essay about AI, smart glasses, and more. That means we can expect more news from Zuckerberg and his team on those topics; perhaps we’ll hear more about Meta’s recently launched Muse AI agent and new glasses hardware. Whatever Zuckerberg and Meta have to say about smart glasses will be particularly notable. The company is dealing with an outpouring of privacy and harassment concerns stemming from the product line’s built-in camera, which has led to them being derided as “pervert glasses.” Meta has already tried to tackle that reputation with recent privacy fixes and a new marketing campaign, but it could introduce more updates on the Connect stage. articles.title: Meta Connect 2026: The biggest news and announcements
articles.summary: Meta’s 2026 Connect event takes place September 23rd and 24th, with news expected about AI, smart glasses, and VR. Follow our coverage here.
articles.body: It’s about time for Meta Connect, the company’s annual product launch event. This year, given the company’s major focus on AI and wearables like smart glasses, it seems likely that we’ll see updates from CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his team on those categories. The company has been facing significant scrutiny because of how some users have been covertly recording other people using the glasses, meaning that one of the biggest announcements of the show could be its rumored camera-free pair. Connect has also traditionally been a venue for updates on Meta’s VR hardware and software. While the company has scaled back its VR ambitions, a recent leak seemingly revealing some kind of unannounced mixed reality glasses could indicate that Meta will show off new immersive headwear technology during the event. Zuckerberg’s keynote is scheduled to begin at 7PM ET / 4PM PT on Wednesday, September 23rd. Follow along with all of our coverage right here.
